Now, the circumference of the heavens is three hundred and sixty-five degrees and one-quarter of a degree. Every day, the sun...
The moon moves one degree per day, plus one-fourth of a degree. In one month,
the moon traverses three hundred and ninety-seven degrees, plus two-fourths of a degree.
The sun travels thirty degrees [per day] and meets with the moon once [in a lunar month].
The constellation [of this conjunction] is the day and time of birth for sentient beings in the four worlds.
The positions where the sun and moon travel constitute their natal mansions (*nakṣatra*).
Furthermore, as the sun completes one circuit through the heavens,
sentient beings reckon it as a year.
When the moon completes one circuit through the heavens,
it constitutes one month for sentient beings;
if the lunar mansions and degrees it reaches contain five stars, [it is known as a conjunction].
One who is in conjunction with the Great Year (Mahāvarṣa), the Five Elements (Pañcabhūta), and the King (Rāja) will certainly give birth to a person of noble rank.
If one is in conjunction with the Moon (Candra) and the Five Elements,
one will likewise give birth to a person of noble rank.
If the moon reaches a lunar station associated with rest, cessation, imprisonment, or death,
those born there will mostly become commoners;
furthermore, if it coincides with the positions of the five planets or with solar and lunar eclipses, the same applies.
In human life, one's birth star (nakṣatra) inevitably manifests signs of good or ill fortune.
Now, the Brahmin monk Kinkuṭa from the Western Regions has received the descent of the deity of the twenty-eighth lunar mansion.
Inquire as to their auspiciousness or misfortune and delineate their forms.
To discern the positions of the seven luminaries and the methods for averting calamities are as follows:

1. The Method for Divining Calamities and Averting Them in the Solar Palace (Ravinaḍī). Regarding the first day reaching its natal lunar mansion and degree: the method for divining calamities and averting them in the Solar Palace is as follows. On the first day, it reaches its natal mansion and degree.
That person shall rightfully receive their due expectations and gain the respect of others;
they shall rightfully obtain rank and emolument.
If they previously possessed transgressions, all shall be entirely remitted.
If the sun is eclipsed while in a person's natal constellation,
that person will immediately encounter the grave calamity of a wind disaster;
one should perform rites to avert it.
Regarding the method for averting [the eclipse], one must first ascertain the exact date of the eclipse.
Five days prior to the eclipse,
one should observe a pure fast and paint the form of the deity.
His form is human with a head resembling that of a lion;
his body is clothed in celestial garments,
he holds a precious vase in his hand, and he is black in color.
One should wear it upon the crown of one's head.
On the day when the natal star (janmanakṣatra) passes away,
cast it into flowing water toward the east, and calamities will naturally disperse.
2. The Method for Divining Calamities and Averting Misfortune in the Lunar Palace. Section Two: The Moon is the essence of the Great Yin (Tàiyīn).
Once every month, it arrives at the natal mansion (*rénmiù*) of human beings.
If one follows the regular course, there will be neither good fortune nor ill fortune;
if one does not follow the regular course, then aberrant phenomena will appear.
Should one commit an offense against the extreme south, there will be calamities and eclipses.
First, one will suffer loss of wife and wealth;
later, one will be granted increased rank and emoluments.
If there is a calamity or eclipse at the extreme north, it will be violated.
It will cause harm to men, women, and male and female slaves.
If one travels slowly, there will be much illness;
if one travels quickly, there will be no calamities or misfortunes.
If the moon’s course deviates from its proper path and there is an impending calamity or eclipse, one must perform rites to avert it.
One should paint the form of a deity.
Its form is like that of a celestial maiden wearing blue heavenly robes and holding a precious sword.
On the night of a lunar eclipse, one should wear it around the neck;
at daybreak, [it will be removed].
If one burns it with pine fire, the calamity will naturally disperse. 3.
The Method for Divining and Averting Calamities in the Wood Palace. Regarding the third [method], the Age Star (Mars) is the son of the Azure Emperor of the East.
The twelve-year cycle completes one revolution of the heavens;
whichever year the person's life star reaches is auspicious.
Reaching the life star during spring brings great good fortune.
If the natal star coincides with the addition of official rank and emoluments, one will obtain wealth and goods.
At the summer solstice, if the natal star coincides, one will give birth to fine sons or daughters.
At the autumn solstice, if the natal star coincides, the person will frequently suffer from illness as well as fractures and injuries.
If one's natal star (mingxing) coincides with the winter solstice, it will bring great good fortune regarding wealth.
If it coincides with the four seasonal nodes (sijizhi), that person will likely encounter empty rumors and the arising of verbal disputes.
If it coincides with the "arrival" of the natal star, calamities will arise.
One should paint the form of a deity;
its shape is like that of a human with a human body and a dragon's head,
wearing celestial garments in colors corresponding to the four seasons.
One should wear it as a neck-strap.
If one's life-force star (mingxiu) has passed its term, discarding it into a mound or a well brings great good fortune. 4.

The Method for Divining and Averting Calamities in the Fire Palace. The fourth section: Regarding the method for divining and averting calamities in the Fire Palace, the planet荧惑 (Yinghuo, Mars) is the son of the Red Emperor of the South.
The second year completes one cycle of the heavens;
when the person's natal star reaches this position, it is generally not auspicious for their life.
When it arrives in spring, the person’s natal star indicates that there will be many sores and ailments upon the bodies of both the man and woman.
As for the person themselves, there will be calamities and pestilence.
At the summer solstice, the life-star (jīvita-tārā) is activated;
such a person will frequently encounter disputes, slander, and matters involving madness.
When autumn arrives, the life-constellation (jīva-nakṣatra) often suffers injury; there will be matters involving weapons and the sword.
One must not ascend to high places, nor should one ride a black donkey or horse.
Do not accept people's wealth, goods, or livestock.
At the winter solstice, when the life-star (mingxing) is active, whatever one does or undertakes will not accord with one's wishes;
money, wealth, and livestock will all be dissipated and scattered.
When the four seasons arrive and the person’s natal star (jīva-nakṣatra) undergoes a shift or change,
if there is misfortune, one should paint the form of a deity;
its shape is like an elephant, black in color, and facing heaven while crying out loudly.
One should wear it around the neck.
Once the fire and the stars have passed,
one should burn it with the wood of the *buddha-gandha* (Boswellia thurifera) and *chou-mu* (Cedrus deodara).
The calamity will then pass. 5.

The Method for Divining Calamities and Averting Them at the Earth-Palace (Tǔgōng). The Method for Divining Calamities and Averting Them at the Earth-Palace, Part Five. As for the Planet of Stability (Zhèn-xīng), it is the son of the Yellow Emperor (Huangdì) of the Central Region.
In twenty-nine years and six months, one completes a full circuit of the heavens.
When it reaches the human life star (*jīvita-nakṣatra*), many sounds of wailing arise among people.
When it reaches the human life star in spring, [the same occurs].
If there are matters of strife, dispute, death, or burial,
one should not see things such as military weapons.
At the summer solstice, the life-star (míng-xīng) is active.
The men and women of this person will frequently suffer from illnesses.
They themselves will face the misfortune of being bound by shackles and chains.
When autumn arrives, there will be matters of loss or disappearance concerning their life-force star (*jīva-tārā*), and all dealings will be unfavorable.
There will be loss of property in water;
at the winter solstice, the life star (jīva-graha) is afflicted,
and sounds of weeping shall arise within that person's household.
When the four seasons arrive at one's life star,
that person is destined to suffer from a serious illness.
To avert it, one should paint the form of a deity.
Its form is like that of a Brahmin riding a black ox;
when the star reaches its natal mansion, one should wear it upon the neck.
Once the star has passed through its natal mansion, [the ritual is complete].
If one burns it with dry wood, the calamity will pass. 6.

The Method for Divining and Averting Calamities According to the *Jin-gong* (Golden Palace). The sixth section on the method for divining and averting calamities according to the *Jin-gong*: Venus is the son of the White Emperor of the West.
The heavens complete one cycle in a year.
Wherever the person’s natal star (mìngxīng) reaches during that cycle, there will be good or bad fortune.
When it reaches the natal star in spring:
That person ought to travel far away;
on the road ten thousand *li* long, there will be illness,
and the household will suffer loss.
At the summer solstice, one’s life star (mingxing) is activated;
it is likely that one's relatives or old friends will suffer death or loss,
and it is also likely that one will have to observe mourning for a superior.
When autumn arrives, it is the person's life star;
that person will encounter military calamities, obstacles in their endeavors, and the sight of blood.
When winter solstice arrives, it is the person's life star.
This person shall preside over great military authority.
When traveling abroad, they will achieve significant gains and benefits.
In the four seasons, their life star (mingxing) will reach its peak.
That person will likely receive bad news;
though possessing a name, they lack a physical form and will engage in much litigation and dispute.
To ward this off, one should paint the image of a deity.
Its form is like that of a celestial maiden (devī), holding a seal (mudrā) and riding a white cock;
one should wear it around the neck.
When the fatal star (antaka-ṛkṣa) passes, one should burn it with fire.
The calamities will surely be dispersed. 7.

The Method for Divining and Averting Calamities in the Water Palace. The Method for Divining and Averting Calamities in the Water Palace, Number Seven: The planet Chenxing (Jupiter) is the son of the Black Emperor of the North.
One year constitutes one full cycle through the heavens;
the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of human life varies according to the natal star reached by this cycle.
When it reaches the natal star in spring, [it brings such results].
Such people often have disputes among their womenfolk, leading to disharmony within the household.
At the summer solstice, the life-star of such individuals is activated;
consequently, many strange phenomena will appear within their dwellings, causing their minds to be unsettled.
There will also be movement;
later, there will be great good fortune.
When autumn arrives, the person's life star indicates they shall receive a change of office and an increase in emolument.
At the winter solstice, if one’s life star (*jīva-tārā*) is afflicted, there will be much illness and the harmonious vital energy (*sāma-vāyu*) will not circulate.
The five viscera (*pañca-dhātu*) will be unsettled, and the spirit and vital breath (*prāṇa*) will be unable to sustain themselves.
This applies to one’s life star when the four seasons arrive.
If a conspiracy arises within the household,
there will be much loss and escape [of wealth].
To subdue this, one should paint the image of a deity.
It has the form of a black snake with four legs and feeds on crabs.
It should be worn as a sash around the neck.

Once the *guoming* (over-life) star has passed, it should be discarded; if not discarded and thrown into flowing water, there will be misfortune. [Note: Regarding the above, the seven luminaries (*qi yao*) bring about many calamities when they reach their respective positions.

When the day reaches the position of Life (Ming-wei), one attains blessings and a portion of deliverance; there is hope for auspicious union and reliance on the numinous transformation to cultivate merit. Be careful regarding anger and delusion; for men and women, there may be illness.

When the day reaches the position of Wealth (Zai-wei), there will be the gathering and dispersal of wealth with minor disputes; be cautious of this, and it will be auspicious. It is auspicious to guard the household.

In the House of Brothers (Gong-you), there is benefit; friends increase and resources are added, which is most auspicious. In the House of Fields and Dwelling (Tian-zhai), there is illness among relatives.

"Diagram" refers to the division of the twelve *rāśis* and the twenty-eight lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*) into degrees.
In constructing the diagram, the Aries (*meṣa*) mansion is made the first, and so forth.
The *Tongyun* states: "Regarding the lords of the three directions, if one was born during the day, one may take [the planets] from whichever mansion the Sun is located;
if one was born at night,"
It is said that one may take [the sign] from whichever palace the moon occupies at midnight, and so forth; one should then determine it by the palace occupied at the time of birth,
filling the subsequent卯 (māu) hour as the upper palace,
and thereby establish it as the natal palace (*janma-rāśi*).
The remaining eleven palaces may be understood by analogy with this.
Thus, the twelve positions fill the celestial cycles and periods;
they vary according to the individual.
